content.text:
Measure whether agents ever actually RAN `entire why` or `entire checkpoint
search` on this machine.

TRAP: a UserPromptSubmit hook injects context quoting both commands verbatim
into every prompt, and both also appear in the CLI's own source, help output,
and PR bodies. A text grep is ~100% false positives. Only count a command in
shell COMMAND POSITION inside a tool call's command field.

Do this in ONE pass — no exploratory greps:
1. Transcripts: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl (includes subagents). Also
   ~/.codex, ~/.copilot, ~/.factory, ~/.gemini, ~/.opencode, ~/.pi if present.
2. DISCOVER the schema, don't assume it: dump which key names hold shell
   commands across a sample. Recurse generically over those keys. Do not
   hardcode one agent's message.content[] -> tool_use -> input.command path;
   Codex stores argv lists like ["bash","-lc","..."] under `command`.
3. Normalize before matching: strip heredoc bodies, blank quoted spans, split
   on `; && || | newline`, strip leading FOO=bar / sudo / `cd x &&`. Match only
   at the START of a resulting segment.
4. Never match tool RESULTS or stdout — help text and diffs live there.
5. Denominator: count transcripts containing the injected hint by testing a
   short distinctive substring against the RAW LINE, not a parsed field. The
   hook context is not stored under message.content.

Deliver:
- real invocation count per target command, with every matching command line
  shown so I can eyeball it
- how many transcripts carried the hint, plus date range
- a census of every `entire <verb>` that WAS invoked (what agents reach for
  instead)
- an explicit list of what you did not scan

I'll measure actual invocations of `entire why` and `entire checkpoint search` across all agent transcripts on this machine, using a single schema-discovering scan that only extracts shell-command fields from tool *calls* (never results or message text).

First, a quick look at what exists and how big it is:

content.text:
All numbers are in. Here's the full picture.

## TLDR: `entire why` has **never** been run by any agent on this machine. `entire checkpoint search` has been run **6 times ever** — and all 6 predate the hint injection. In the 21 transcripts that actually carried the injected hint (Jul 23 → Aug 11), neither command was invoked once.

## Real invocations, every matching line

**`entire why`: 0.** The verb `why` does not appear even once across the census of 4,606 real `entire` invocations.

**`entire checkpoint search`: 6** (4 Claude Code, 2 Codex):

| when | agent | command line (verbatim, truncated) |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-15 | codex | `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go run ./cmd/entire checkpoint search --help` |
| 2026-06-18 | codex | `./scripts/entire-dev checkpoint search 5dbcd2da-0a2d-488a-a2e6-1d63a2b98e94` |
| 2026-07-14 | claude | `entire checkpoint search "headless keyring hint file token store" 2>&1 \| head -12` |
| 2026-07-14 | claude | `entire checkpoint search "headless keyring hint file token store" 2>&1 \| python3 -c "…parse results…"` |
| 2026-07-14 | claude | `sleep 20; entire checkpoint search "loose permissions warning tokenstore file backend" 2>&1 \| python3 -c "…"` |
| 2026-07-20 | claude | `entire checkpoint search --help 2>&1 \| head -30; echo ===; ls …demo-repository …; entire auth status …` |

Note two of the six are `--help` probes, not searches, and the July 14 trio is one session hammering the same query. Real usage is effectively ~3 searches in one debugging session plus one UUID lookup.

## Denominator: the hint

**21 transcripts** carried the injected hint (substring test `"recover the intent behind existing code"` against raw lines): 15 in `~/.claude/projects`, 6 in `~/.codex/sessions`. Date range **2026-07-23 → 2026-08-11**. Every one of the 6 target invocations is *older* than the earliest hint-carrying transcript — so the measured conversion rate of the hint itself is **0/21**. (Caveat: if the hook's wording differed before Jul 23, older hint-carrying transcripts wouldn't match this substring; the July 14–20 searches may have been driven by an earlier wording or by the user directly.)

## What agents actually reach for (`entire <verb>` census, deduplicated)

4,606 total invocations, 88 distinct verb phrases. Split into what matters:

**Infrastructure noise (not agent choice):** `hooks claude-code` 1,867 (the hook binary itself, recorded in transcripts' `hookInfos[].command`), plus `hooks copilot-cli` 24, `hooks git` 8, `hooks codex` 6. Another 15 hook-command hits found inside `settings.json`-type files were excluded entirely.

**Deliberate agent/user usage, top of the list:**

| verb | count | | verb | count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trail finding` | 879 | | `agent-help` | 60 |
| `trail show` | 127 | | `repo mirror` | 52 |
| `explain` | 104 | | `trail list` | 51 |
| `review` | 101 | | `checkpoint list` | 50 |
| `search` (top-level) | 90 | | `checkpoint tokens` | 47 |
| `status` | 90 | | `trail update` | 41 |
| `trail` (other) | 86 | | `session current` | 40 |
| `auth status` | 84 | | `--help` | 40 |
| `checkpoint explain` | 77 | | `login` | 39 |
| `version` | 73 | | `session attach` | 32 |
| `recap` | 72 | | *…plus ~60 more, long tail* | |

The interesting substitution story: for the exact job the hint advertises, agents use **`entire explain`** (104) / **`checkpoint explain`** (77) and the top-level **`entire search`** shortcut (90) — the shortcut, never the canonical `checkpoint search` form the hint quotes. `why` is untouched.

Minor census noise: a handful of tokenizer artifacts like `doctor 2>`, `auth token)`, `trail 613` (~10 entries) where redirects/IDs landed in the verb slot — they're real invocations of `doctor`, `trail <id>`, etc., just mislabeled.

## How the trap was avoided (method)

Schema was discovered, not assumed — command-bearing key paths found and used: `message.content[].input.command` (Claude, incl. subagent sidechains), `payload.command` + `payload.arguments*.cmd` (Codex, argv lists and JSON-string arguments both unwrapped, `["bash","-lc",…]` scripts extracted), `data.arguments.command` / `data.toolRequests[].arguments.command` (Copilot), `messages[].toolCalls[].args.command` (Gemini). Result contexts (`toolUseResult`, `type:tool_result`/`function_call_output`, `output`/`stdout` keys — 51+ command-shaped fields) were structurally excluded. Commands were normalized (heredocs stripped, quoted spans blanked, split on `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`/newline/`` ` ``/`$(`, leading env-assignments/`sudo`/`timeout`/`cd x &&` removed) and matched only at segment start, accepting `entire`, `entire-dev`, path-prefixed forms, and `go run ./cmd/entire`. 634 duplicate copies (Codex `parsed_cmd` mirrors, parent-transcript progress echoes) were deduplicated by (command, timestamp).

Scanned: 5,264 files / ~1.44GB of JSON(L) — claude 821 files, codex 1,480, copilot 368, factory 525, gemini 2,054, opencode 15, pi 1.

## Explicitly not scanned

- **OpenCode's real data dir** `~/.local/share/opencode` — only the near-empty `~/.opencode` (15 files) was in scope as specified; if OpenCode was used seriously, its transcripts live in the XDG path.
- **Cursor** (`~/Library/Application Support/Cursor`), **Antigravity**, **Claude Desktop**, and any IDE-GUI chat logs — not in the requested roots.
- **Non-JSON files** under the scanned roots (`config.toml`, `.log`, `.md`, shell history) — so a human typing the command in a plain terminal (zsh/fish history) is invisible to this measurement.
- **202 unparseable JSON lines/files** (201 gemini, 1 copilot) were skipped after the raw-line hint test.
- **Nested-shell edge cases**: `bash -c "…"` string form was unwrapped one level only; commands smuggled through `xargs`/`eval "$VAR"` wouldn't match (none were observed near-missing).
- **Deleted/rotated transcripts** — this measures what survives on disk today.

Full machine-readable report with every schema path, census entry, and match location: `scratchpad/report.json`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The measurement exposes a discoverability gap worth acting on: agents *do* use Entire's recall surface heavily (`explain`, `search`, `checkpoint explain` — ~270 combined) but reach for it via the verbs they discovered organically, not the two commands the UserPromptSubmit hook quotes. The hint's 0/21 conversion since Jul 23 suggests either the hint's phrasing doesn't map to moments agents recognize ("before large edits"), or agents satisfy the same need through `entire search`/`explain` first and never fall through to `why`/`checkpoint search`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
